title: Giving change
examples: If I pay with a ten euro note, how much change should I get back?
Can you show me how to count up to the amount I paid?
What is the difference between paying and getting change?

explain.say: Change is the money you get back. You get change when you pay more than the price.

items: Change: the money you get back
You pay more than the price

explain.say: You can find the change by counting up. Start at the price. Count up to the money you paid.

items: Count up to what you paid

explain.say: A toy costs three euro. You pay with five euro. Count up from three: four, five. That is two jumps. So your change is two euro.
You can also take away. Take the price away from the money you paid.
A book costs four euro. You pay with ten euro. Ten take away four is six. Your change is six euro.
Check your change. The price and the change together make the money you paid.

faq.a: Change is the extra money you receive when you pay with more than the actual price. It is the difference between what you paid and what something cost.
No, you can count up or take away. Both ways give the same change.
asks: Is counting up the only way?

faq.q: When do I need to calculate change?
faq.a: You find the change when you give more money than the price. This happens in shops.

faq.q: If I pay with a ten euro note, how do I know the change?
faq.a: Count up from the price to ten euro. If it costs seven euro, count eight, nine, ten. That is three jumps, so you get three euro change.
asks: How do I count up to ten?
What if I pay with a twenty dollar bill?

faq.q: Is subtraction always easier for change?
faq.a: Use the way you find easier. Taking away is quick for small numbers. Counting up lets you see each step.

facts: Change is the money returned after a purchase.
Counting up involves starting at the price and counting to the paid amount.
Subtraction finds the difference between two numbers.
If the paid amount equals the cost, you get zero change.

quiz.say: A pencil costs two euro. You pay five euro. Tap your change.
quiz.why: Count up from 2: 3, 4, 5. That is three jumps, so your change is €3.

wrong.0: Seven euro is the price and the money added together.
wrong.1: Start at 2 and count only the jumps: 3, 4, 5 makes three jumps.

quiz.say: A ball costs six euro. You pay ten euro. Tap your change.
quiz.why: Ten take away six is four. So your change is €4.

wrong.0: Sixteen euro is €6 and €10 added together, but change means taking away.
wrong.2: Count up from 6: 7, 8, 9, 10 makes four jumps.

quiz.say: A hat costs eight euro. You pay twenty euro. Tap your change.
quiz.why: From 8 to 10 is 2, and from 10 to 20 is 10 more. So your change is €12.

wrong.0: Count up from 8 to 10 first, which is 2 more, and then add the 10.
wrong.1: Twenty-eight euro is the price and the money added together, and change is less than what you paid.
